annotations.text:
The Coach line replaces the Training Insights teaser one-for-one — same slot, same height band.

The difference is that it always says something. The old teaser was blank until a rule fired, which is what taught people to stop tapping it.

One tap down, not a tab. Charts keeps its slot.

TODAY is register A. WORTH KNOWING holds the cards. INSIGHTS is the describing layer, kept as its own word so a declining chart reads as a mirror rather than criticism.

Performance-vs-expected lives here first, not on the summary sheet — you are browsing days later rather than being handed a verdict while you pack your bag.

Every sentence has the app as its subject. Below plan = the app was high. Above = you were strong.

Five cards in the existing InsightCardView grammar.

The third is the one the whole design rests on: it acquires intent by naming an observed pattern and asking whether it is wanted — no onboarding questionnaire.

Decision C in the scoping doc, drawn rather than argued. Same scenario, two voices.

States is shippable now and stops one step short of useful. Tells is what a lifter would actually use, and it needs a write path that does not exist yet — plus it makes the app the author of the recommendation.

Week one, and the honest cost of dropping the onboarding questions: nothing here comments on training shape, because there is nothing yet to comment on.

No findings section at all — absent, not empty-stated. No progress bars toward unlocking.
